title: maataa-os.allb.xyz is now the home of MAATAA OS
body: This site replaces the earlier concept page. It now holds the vision and planned product directions, the roadmap, an FAQ, support and security reporting, and the team page with the roles opening after the seed round. Releases, board runs and decisions are posted here first, and in the RSS feed.

title: Board runs for alpha.9: power cuts, priority inheritance, Panini 10
body: Run on the NUCLEO-F411RE with the development key.
points: Store survives power loss: three runs, 9 USB cable pulls during writes; each time key 63 held the last acknowledged value or the one in flight. All PASS.

Priority inheritance: with it, the high-priority task gets the lock before the middle one finishes; without it, the low task starves holding the lock. Both kernels behaved as expected; the normal kernel was flashed back.
Panini capsule 10 installed by a signed commit: hare + iha gives hara iha (rule 10, 8.3.19), the same as the host library.

title: Release 0.1.0-alpha.9
body: Evidence release for QEMU and the NUCLEO-F411RE. System calls, the host-channel protocol and the sandhi wire format are unchanged.
points: Sandhi: 8.3.19 after ayadi; e and ai drop the y, o and au keep the v.
The store-full error is now checked through the system call itself.
A CI check compares the docs with the code on every push; QEMU smoke test 15 of 15.

title: Release 0.1.0-alpha.8: signed host requests
points: Committing an app install, removing the installed app and writing a task's store key now need an ed25519 signature over a fresh per-boot challenge, so recorded requests cannot be replayed.
Each store key is written only by its owner: the host channel, or an app by its signed name. Reads stay open by design.

title: Release 0.1.0-alpha.7: consolidation
body: No change to system calls or the wire format.
points: Engineering docs written from the source: system-call ABI, memory map, threat model, rule and evidence registries.
Code no build used was removed, and more smoke checks were added, including MPU faults.

title: Release 0.1.0-alpha.6: Panini capsule 8
body: New sandhi rules in both the capsule and the host library, and a release script that refuses to create a missing signing key by accident.

title: CAN driver for the NUCLEO-F446RE
body: The first driver for the Field I/O family. It is in the kernel and tested on the host and in CI; it has not run on a board yet. The F446 board arrives this week.
points: bxCAN1 at 500 kbit/s. Only exact bit timings are accepted (42 MHz bus, 14 time quanta per bit), checked by 8 host tests.
At boot the F446 kernel runs a loopback self-test: two frames go out and come back unchanged, and a frame the filters must block is checked to stay out.
The board test script fails unless the self-test line is in the boot log.
CI now builds with the same compiler as the size table (rustc 1.91.0).

title: Modbus and battery data in the store; RS-485 driver core
body: Groundwork for energy meters and battery packs. Tested on the host and in QEMU; not yet on a board.
points: Two new store owners, Modbus and BMS. Each has flash keys for settings and RAM-only keys for live readings, so a reading every second does not wear out the flash.
Only the owning signed app can write its live keys; a signed host request cannot.
RS-485 driver core: line settings, baud rate and Modbus RTU frame gaps (3.5 characters, or 1,750 µs above 19,200 baud), with 13 host tests.

title: The roadmap now covers the whole portfolio
body: The roadmap has three parts: what the operating system must do (done, now to January 2027, next, later), the products by family and tier, and research kept separate. The second chip family is the STM32H5, then the STM32G4. Sections and the 112 portfolio concepts now have icons.
